articles.title: Joe Rogan renews multimillion-dollar podcast deal with Spotify
articles.summary: Spotify announced that it has renewed its deal with Joe Rogan, who heads the audio company's most popular podcast.
articles.body:
Spotify on Thursday said it had renewed its deal with Joe Rogan, who leads the audio company's most popular podcast, "The Joe Rogan Experience."

The podcast, which has 18 million followers on Spotify, has been the company's top podcast since 2020. The terms of the multiyear licensing deal were not disclosed. The Wall Street Journal , citing unnamed sources, reported the deal had an estimated earnout of $250 million.

"The partnership with Spotify has been an amazing fit, and they're incredible to work with," Rogan said in a statement. "I'm extremely happy and excited to continue with them for years to come."

Rogan first entered into an exclusive multiyear podcast deal with Spotify in 2020 in a deal said to be worth $100 million . The partnership was key to driving podcast audiences to Spotify, which at the time was mostly known as a streaming music service.

In 2024, the company extended its partnership for "The Joe Rogan Experience" to be distributed on other platforms, and that will continue in the latest deal. Rogan's show was ranked as the top podcast last year on Spotify, YouTube and Apple Podcasts.

"Joe has built something incredibly enduring, and his show continues to resonate with a massive global audience because there's simply nothing else like it," said Jordan Newman, head of content partnerships at Spotify, in a statement.

"The Joe Rogan Experience" has run into controversy, spurring a Spotify boycott in 2022 led by Neil Young over concerns that Rogan and his guests were spreading misinformation related to COVID-19 vaccines. Rogan also received criticism over his use of the N-word on past episodes of his show, for which he later apologized.

After the backlash, Spotify posted its content moderation rules and said it would add content advisory labels on COVID-related podcasts. Rogan also said he would do a better job of balancing different perspectives.

Young later returned to Spotify in 2024.

This story originally appeared in Los Angeles Times .

articles.title: Braskem tem até esta sexta para avançar em acordo sobre dívida de R$ 56 bilhões; maior credor ainda não aderiu | G1
articles.standfirst: Empresa, acionistas e credores tentam definir condições para reestruturar dívidas em recuperação extrajudicial. Braskem já tem apoio de 39,6% dos créditos envolvidos, mas precisa superar 50% até novembro para avançar com o plano.
articles.summary: A petroquímica precisa avançar nas negociações para reestruturar US$ 10,9 bilhões em dívidas; Banco de Nova York Mellon, com R$ 36,4 bilhões a receber, está entre os credores.
articles.body:
A Braskem tem até esta sexta-feira (9) para que seus principais acionistas e credores cheguem a um acordo sobre as condições comerciais do plano de recuperação extrajudicial da empresa, que prevê a renegociação de US$ 10,9 bilhões (R$ 56,5 bilhões) em dívidas.

A empresa, seus principais acionistas — Petrobras e FIP Shine I — e os credores que já aderiram ao processo precisam chegar a um consenso sobre os termos do plano. Segundo a Braskem, os termos da negociação estão em andamento e sendo discutidos entre as partes.

"A companhia permanece empenhada em buscar uma solução consensual e ordenada para sua reestruturação financeira e manterá o mercado informado sobre os próximos passos, no momento adequado", afirma a Braskem em nota ao g1.

Apesar de o prazo estar chegando ao fim, ele não encerra a recuperação extrajudicial. A Braskem ainda terá 90 dias, contados do protocolo do pedido, em 24 de agosto, para conquistar novas adesões e obter o apoio de mais de 50% dos credores abrangidos pelo processo. (saiba mais abaixo)

Ou seja, hoje é uma data decisiva para que a companhia avance nas negociações de sua dívida com os credores. Sem um acordo, há o risco de encerramento das tratativas, o que pode aumentar a pressão sobre a empresa e abrir caminho para um pedido de falência.

Já o prazo de 90 dias, que termina em meados de novembro, é o limite legal para que a Braskem obtenha o apoio necessário à aprovação de seu plano de recuperação extrajudicial.

Atualmente, os signatários representam 39,6% do total.

🔍 Na recuperação extrajudicial , a empresa negocia diretamente com seus credores uma forma de reorganizar as dívidas e depois leva o acordo à Justiça para homologação. É diferente da recuperação judicial , que envolve um processo mais amplo na Justiça. O acordo pode prever, por exemplo, mais prazo para pagar as dívidas ou um período sem pagamentos. Nos dois casos, o objetivo é evitar a falência e dar condições para que a empresa continue funcionando.

O que acontece se houver acordo nesta sexta-feira?

O acordo deve definir os princípios comerciais que vão orientar a elaboração da versão atualizada do plano de recuperação.

A proposta prevê a divisão dos sacrifícios financeiros entre os credores, a empresa e seus acionistas controladores.

Alterações nos prazos de pagamento das dívidas;

Períodos de carência para o pagamento do valor principal e dos juros;

Possíveis melhorias nas garantias e nas condições financeiras oferecidas aos credores.

O plano também prevê a possibilidade de converter parte da dívida em ações da companhia. Se isso ocorrer, a participação dos atuais acionistas poderá ser reduzida.

O pedido apresentado pela Braskem informa um passivo total de R$ 187,07 bilhões . No entanto, a maior parte desse valor não entra no cálculo da recuperação extrajudicial.

Desse total, R$ 130,6 bilhões correspondem a dívidas entre empresas do próprio grupo, chamadas de créditos intercompany. O valor representa cerca de 70% do passivo informado e foi excluído da base de cálculo do apoio dos credores.

A dívida efetivamente incluída na recuperação extrajudicial soma R$ 56,48 bilhões , o equivalente a US$ 10,9 bilhões em obrigações financeiras quirografárias.

🔎 A expressão significa, neste caso, dívidas financeiras que não contam com uma garantia específica sobre determinado bem. Nesse grupo estão títulos de dívida emitidos no exterior e contratos bancários.

Por que a Braskem entrou em recuperação extrajudicial?

A situação financeira da companhia foi pressionada por três fatores principais: os custos relacionados ao desastre geológico em Maceió (AL), as baixas margens no setor petroquímico global e o elevado endividamento financeiro.

O processo envolve seis empresas do grupo: a Braskem S.A. e cinco subsidiárias financeiras e operacionais no exterior.

A Justiça autorizou que as seis empresas sejam tratadas conjuntamente no processo. Essa estrutura, chamada de consolidação substancial, permite que os ativos e as dívidas das companhias sejam considerados em conjunto para determinados efeitos da recuperação.

A Braskem justificou o pedido pela gestão centralizada no Brasil, pelo controle comum das empresas, pela existência de garantias entre elas e pela atuação coordenada no mercado petroquímico.

A análise da NEOT Tecnologia, especializada em dados sobre recuperação judicial e insolvência, aponta essa questão como um dos pontos juridicamente mais vulneráveis do processo.

Segundo a avaliação, credores contrários ao processo podem questionar o cálculo conjunto das adesões, já que o percentual de 39,6% não é alcançado individualmente por todas as empresas, especialmente pelas subsidiárias no exterior.

A Braskem apresentou o pedido com o apoio de credores que representam R$ 22,38 bilhões, o equivalente a 39,6% dos créditos incluídos na recuperação.

Entre os signatários estão o Grupo Ad Hoc de Bondholders, formado por detentores de títulos de dívida emitidos no exterior, e instituições como Barclays Bank , Banco Santander , Citibank e Pentágono DTVM .

Os credores que ainda não aderiram representam os 60,4% restantes, equivalentes a cerca de R$ 34,09 bilhões. A Braskem precisa conquistar novas adesões para superar a maioria exigida por lei.

Entre as instituições que ainda podem aderir ao plano estão Itaú Unibanco , BNP Paribas , Crédit Agricole , Sumitomo Mitsui , Deutsche Bank , KfW IPEX-Bank , Natixis , Mizuho Bank , Bladex , DEG , DZ Bank , Standard Chartered Bank e Eco Securitizadora .

Os cinco maiores credores financeiros de mercado (excluindo intercompany):

The Bank of New York Mellon (BNY Mellon): R$ 36,44 bilhões (20,47% do total global)

Pentágono S.A. DTVM: R$ 2,24 bilhões (1,26% do total global)

Banco Santander S.A.: R$ 2,23 bilhões (1,25% do total global)

Barclays Bank PLC: R$ 1,80 bilhão (1,01% do total global)

Sumitomo Mitsui Banking Corporation (SMBC): R$ 1,11 bilhão (0,62% do total global)

Mesmo que as partes cheguem a um acordo sobre os princípios comerciais do plano nesta sexta-feira (9), a recuperação extrajudicial ainda terá outras etapas.

A Braskem tem 90 dias , contados do protocolo do pedido, em 24 de agosto, para obter o apoio de mais da metade dos créditos abrangidos pela recuperação. O prazo termina em 22 de novembro.

A versão atualizada do plano deverá ser apresentada à Justiça. Os credores poderão contestar a proposta, e a Braskem e as demais empresas envolvidas terão de responder aos questionamentos.

Na sequência, o Ministério Público analisará o processo antes de a Justiça decidir se homologa ou rejeita o plano.

Se a Braskem alcançar a maioria exigida e a Justiça homologar o plano, as condições aprovadas passarão a valer para todos os credores abrangidos, inclusive os que não aderiram à proposta.

Se a Braskem não obtiver a maioria necessária dentro dos 90 dias, a legislação permite que a empresa peça a conversão do processo em recuperação judicial.

articles.title: Trump cria comitê para investigar Lisa Cook, diretora do Fed, diz Casa Branca | G1
articles.standfirst: Comitê deverá apurar acusações contra a diretora do banco central americano e informar ao presidente se há justa causa para sua destituição.
articles.summary: Comitê deverá apurar acusações contra a diretora do banco central americano e informar ao presidente se há justa causa para sua destituição.
articles.body:
Montagem mostra Lisa Cook e Donald Trump — Foto: SAUL LOEB and ANDREW CABALLERO-REYNOLDS / AFP

O presidente dos Estados Unidos, Donald Trump , anunciou a criação de um comitê para investigar Lisa Cook, diretora do Federal Reserve ( Fed ), o banco central americano, segundo um comunicado publicado no site da Casa Branca nesta sexta-feira (9).

“Para me auxiliar no cumprimento dessa responsabilidade, o comitê deverá investigar as acusações contra a diretora Cook e me informar se há ‘justa causa’ para sua destituição”, diz o comunicado, datado de 7 de outubro.

O comitê realizará uma audiência presencial na Casa Branca “para analisar as provas e as acusações contra a diretora”, segundo o memorando presidencial. O documento estabelece que a audiência terá duração máxima de quatro horas.

A criação do comitê é mais um passo na tentativa de Trump de retirar Cook do cargo . Trump já havia tentado demitir Cook em 2025 , acusando-a de cometer fraudes hipotecárias, o que ela nega.

A diretora, que é a primeira mulher negra a ocupar esse posto no Fed , afirmou que as acusações eram um pretexto de Trump para afastá-la do cargo por divergências sobre a condução da política monetária.

Em junho deste ano, a Suprema Corte dos Estados Unidos bloqueou temporariamente sua demissão , por entender que o presidente não havia garantido a ela as condições previstas em lei para contestar as acusações.

Em agosto, a Casa Branca retomou a ofensiva e enviou uma carta à diretora, informando que Trump considerava afastá-la. O documento deu a Cook três semanas para responder as acusações. Na ocasião, seu advogado, Abbe D. Lowell, classificou as alegações como “sem fundamento” e afirmou que não havia causa válida para a demissão.

Ao barrar temporariamente a demissão, por 5 votos a 4, a Suprema Corte não analisou se as acusações eram verdadeiras. A decisão determinou que Cook deveria ter a oportunidade de se defender e devolveu o caso às instâncias inferiores da Justiça.

Cook foi nomeada para a diretoria do Fed em 2022 pelo então presidente Joe Biden, do Partido Democrata, e reconduzida em 2023 para um mandato que vai até 2038.

Desde a criação do banco central americano, em 1913, nenhum outro presidente havia tentado retirar um governador do Federal Reserve.

articles.title: Exportações brasileiras de carne bovina para os EUA sobem 524%  | G1
articles.standfirst: Mesmo com alta de 524% nas vendas de carne bovina em setembro, exportações brasileiras aos EUA caíram 6,5% no acumulado do ano, para US$ 27,5 bilhões, em meio ao tarifaço de Trump.
articles.summary: Mesmo com alta de 524% nas vendas de carne bovina em setembro, exportações brasileiras aos EUA caíram 6,5% no acumulado do ano, para US$ 27,5 bilhões, em meio ao tarifaço de Trump.
articles.body:
As exportações brasileiras de carne bovina para os Estados Unidos dispararam 524,3% em setembro, na comparação com o mesmo mês de 2025, segundo levantamento da Câmara Americana de Comércio para o Brasil (Amcham).

O avanço, porém, não foi suficiente para reverter a queda das vendas brasileiras ao mercado americano no acumulado do ano , em um período marcado pelas sobretaxas impostas pelo governo de Donald Trump a produtos brasileiros.

De janeiro a setembro, as exportações do Brasil para os Estados Unidos somaram US$ 27,5 bilhões, uma queda de 6,5% em relação ao mesmo período do ano passado.

O valor representa uma redução de US$ 1,9 bilhão e é o menor para os nove primeiros meses do ano desde 2023.

Em setembro, entretanto, houve recuperação. As exportações brasileiras para os americanos alcançaram US$ 3,5 bilhões, alta de 31,9% em relação ao mesmo mês de 2025.

O crescimento foi impulsionado tanto pelo aumento da quantidade de produtos vendidos, de 3,1%, quanto pela elevação de 28% no preço médio das mercadorias exportadas.

🔎 O salto da carne bovina ocorreu em meio às sobretaxas aplicadas pelos Estados Unidos a produtos brasileiros. O item está entre as exceções às tarifas adicionais impostas pelo presidente americano, assim como café solúvel, mel orgânico e pescados, como a tilápia.

Carne bovina dispara, enquanto outros produtos recuam

O desempenho positivo da carne também aparece no acumulado do ano. Entre janeiro e setembro, as vendas de carne bovina ao mercado americano cresceram 82,9%, alcançando US$ 1,72 bilhão.

"Além da cota adicional de importação iniciada em setembro, a demanda dos EUA é impulsionada pela restrição na oferta interna de gado, consequência da fase de baixa do ciclo pecuário americano", explica a Associação Brasileira das Indústrias Exportadoras de Carnes (ABIEC).

O resultado contrasta com o de outros produtos importantes da pauta exportadora brasileira.

No mesmo período, as vendas de petróleo bruto aos Estados Unidos caíram 35,8%, enquanto as de café não torrado recuaram 20% .

As exportações de produtos semiacabados de ferro, que ainda precisam passar por outras etapas de fabricação antes de se tornarem produtos finais, diminuíram 4,3%.

Exportações brasileiras perdem força nos principais setores

A queda das vendas aos Estados Unidos também aparece nos três grandes setores da economia :

Indústria de transformação, que reúne produtos industrializados.

Entre janeiro e setembro, as exportações brasileiras para o mercado americano recuaram 17,8% na agropecuária, 32% na indústria extrativa e 1,2% na indústria de transformação.

O desempenho foi diferente nos demais mercados internacionais. Excluídos os Estados Unidos, as exportações brasileiras cresceram 8,9% na agropecuária, 21,2% na indústria extrativa e 6,3% na indústria de transformação.

Apesar da retração, os produtos industrializados continuaram concentrando a maior parte das vendas brasileiras aos americanos, com 84,4% do total exportado entre janeiro e setembro .

A queda de 1,2% nas exportações desse setor foi a primeira para o período desde 2020, ano marcado pela pandemia de COVID-19. Mesmo assim, os Estados Unidos permaneceram como o principal destino dos produtos industrializados brasileiros, à frente da União Europeia, da China e do Mercosul.

Produtos sobretaxados acumulam perdas no ano

As exportações de produtos brasileiros sujeitos a tarifas adicionais dos Estados Unidos também apresentaram recuperação em setembro, mas continuam em queda no acumulado de 2026.

No mês, as vendas desses produtos cresceram 28,1% em valor, para US$ 1,46 bilhão. Entre os itens submetidos às tarifas mais elevadas, de 25% a 37,5%, a alta foi de 27,8%, para US$ 466,5 milhões.

De janeiro a setembro, porém, as exportações desse último grupo recuaram 25,4%, o equivalente a US$ 1,4 bilhão a menos em vendas.

Entre os dez produtos mais exportados aos Estados Unidos sujeitos a tarifas adicionais de 25% ou 37,5%, nove registraram queda no acumulado do ano. As maiores retrações citadas incluem:

Madeira de coníferas , com recuo de 50,6%;

Granitos trabalhados , com queda de 34,1%; e

Importações dos Estados Unidos crescem pelo terceiro mês seguido

Na direção oposta à das exportações , as importações brasileiras de produtos americanos voltaram a crescer em setembro. As compras somaram US$ 4,43 bilhões, alta de 2,1% em relação ao mesmo mês de 2025. Foi o terceiro mês consecutivo de crescimento, após sete meses de queda.

O avanço foi puxado principalmente pelos combustíveis, cujas importações aumentaram 108,5% em setembro. Entre janeiro e setembro, as compras brasileiras dessa categoria totalizaram US$ 6,86 bilhões, alta de 68,5% na comparação anual.

Apesar da recuperação mensal, as importações totais de produtos americanos caíram 7,1% no acumulado do ano, para US$ 31,8 bilhões.

Com as importações superiores às exportações, o Brasil acumulou déficit comercial de US$ 4,3 bilhões com os Estados Unidos nos nove primeiros meses do ano .

O resultado negativo, que indica que o país comprou mais do que vendeu ao mercado americano, foi 10,8% menor do que o registrado no mesmo período de 2025.

articles.title: Ibovespa opera em alta e vai aos 209 mil pontos, com inflação e eleições no foco; dólar cai | G1
articles.standfirst: Na véspera, a moeda americana subiu 0,27%, cotada a R$ R$ 5,0242. Já a bolsa brasileira avançou 0,94%, aos 206.220 pontos.
articles.summary: Na véspera, a moeda americana subiu 0,27%, cotada a R$ R$ 5,0242. Já a bolsa brasileira avançou 0,94%, aos 206.220 pontos.
articles.body:
O dólar opera em queda nesta sexta-feira (9), com um recuo de 0,84% perto das 12h30, cotado a R$ 4,9822 . Já o Ibovespa , principal índice da bolsa brasileira, tinha alta de 1,41% no mesmo horário, aos 209.135 pontos .

▶️A inflação brasileira é o principal destaque da sessão. O indicador subiu 0,82% em setembro , após a deflação de 0,32% registrada no mês anterior. O avanço foi puxado principalmente por Habitação, por conta do fim do bônus de Itaipu nas contas de eletricidade, e por Transportes, com aumento das passagens aéreas e dos combustíveis. Na agenda internacional, dados de confiança do consumidor dos Estados Unidos ficam no radar.

▶️ No cenário eleitoral, novas pesquisas eleitorais indicaram vantagem de Flávio Bolsonaro no 2º turno. Segundo a pesquisa Datafolha, o candidato do PL deve ficar com 49% das intenções de voto no segundo turno, enquanto Lula (PT) deve ficar com 45%. Leia mais.

▶️ As incertezas sobre o conflito no Oriente Médio também continuam a influenciar os preços do petróleo no mercado internacional. Na véspera, Donald Trump afirmou que não atacaria o Irã antes das eleições de meio mandato, citando conversa "produtivas" com Teerã. Ainda assim, o bloqueio naval às exportações iranianas e os novos ataques a petroleiros no Estreito de Ormuz continuam a trazer dúvidas sobre a duração do conflito e sobre os impactos nos preços de energia globais.

Com isso, os preços do petróleo tinham volatilidade nesta sexta-feira. Perto das 12h30, o barril do Brent , referência internacional, subia 0,58%, cotado a US$ 104,89 . Já o West Texas Intermediate ( WTI ), referência dos EUA, avançava 0,47% , a US$ 91,92 o barril.

Veja abaixo mais detalhes do dia no mercado.

A primeira pesquisa Datafolha do 2º turno mostra que Flávio Bolsonaro (PL) tem 49% das intenções de voto, contra 45% de Lula (PT). O Datafolha diz que a distância de quatro pontos entre eles configura um empate técnico no limite da margem de erro, que é de 2 pontos percentuais para mais ou para menos, com maior probabilidade de Flávio Bolsonaro estar à frente.

Em votos válidos, Flávio Bolsonaro tem 52%, e Lula, 48%. O levantamento foi encomendado pela Globo e pela Folha de S.Paulo.

A pesquisa também indicou que 49% dos eleitores desaprovam o governo do presidente Lula (PT), candidato à reeleição, enquanto 48% aprovam.

A pesquisa anterior, divulgada há uma semana, mostrava cenário idêntico: 49% desaprovavam e 48% aprovavam o governo.

O Datafolha ouviu 2.520 pessoas de 16 anos ou mais entre os dias 6 e 7 de outubro. A margem de erro é de dois pontos percentuais, para mais ou para menos, e o nível de confiança é de 95%. O número de registro da pesquisa na Justiça Eleitoral é BR-0949/2026.

Nos Estados Unidos, os três principais índices de Wall Street operavam em alta nesta sexta-feira, de olho nos preços do petróleo e ações do setor de telecomunicações.

Perto das 12h30, o Dow Jones subia 0,50%, enquanto o S&P 500 avançava 0,43% e o Nasdaq Composite tinha alta de 0,46%.

Na Europa , o dia também era majoritariamente positivo. No mesmo horário, o DAX , da Alemanha, tinha ganhos de 1,20% e o CAC-40 , da França, subia 0,98%, enquanto o FTSE 100 , do Reino Unido, avançava 1,15%.

Na Ásia , os mercados fecharam mistos nesta sexta-feira, em uma semana de negócios reduzida por feriados em alguns dos principais índices acionários da região. Uma onda de vendas de ações relacionadas à inteligência artificial influenciou parte dos mercados da região.

O SSEC , índice de Xangai, subiu 0,05%, enquanto o CSI300 , índice que reúne as maiores companhias listadas em Xangai e Shenzen, avançou 0,16%. Entre os demais índices da região, o Nikkei , do Japão, recuou 0,02% e o Hang Seng , de Hong Kong, valorizou 1,79%.

O Kospi , da Coreia do Sul e o Taiex , de Taiwan, permaneceram fechados.

articles.title: Investors Pour Into Cash and Set to Stay, BofA’s Hartnett Says
articles.summary: Investors just poured money into cash funds at the fastest pace since the pandemic, and are unlikely to shift it anytime soon, according to Bank of America C...
articles.body:
(Bloomberg) -- Investors just poured money into cash funds at the fastest pace since the pandemic, and are unlikely to shift it anytime soon, according to Bank of America Corp.'s Michael Hartnett.

The large amount of cash on the sidelines is set to stay there until there is "big monetary easing" and sustained interest-rate cuts by the Federal Reserve, the strategist wrote in a note Friday. Money-market funds had inflows of $166.4 billion in the week ended Oct. 7, the most since April 2020.

"No rate cuts, no cash cuts," Hartnett wrote.

The bond market expects another three rate hikes in the US by the end of July, with the next expected at the December meeting. Large reductions in cash holdings tend to coincide with instances of big monetary easing, Harnett wrote.

Stocks face increasing competition from bonds and cash, safer investments with appealing yields, as interest rates rise globally in the face of inflation. Bonds saw a $33.8 billion inflow in the latest week, while $12.4 billion flowed into equities, according to BofA.

Hartnett views the US midterms as the most likely reason for a big move in stocks going into 2027, an event that he's taking a risk-off stance ahead given the current central-bank rate cycle and tighter financial conditions.

articles.title: Wealthy Americans are ditching the 401(k) plans used by 70M workers — here’s where their money is going instead
articles.summary: Maxing out your 401(k) is incredibly common financial advice — but could it be the wrong move?
articles.body:

You've probably heard the advice a thousand times from financial professionals: Max out your 401(k). And there's a good reason for that advice.

On the surface, a 401(k) seems like the perfect account. Money goes into it right from your paycheck, your employer may match contributions and it comes with tax benefits. So it's no surprise that an estimated 71.5 million American workers (1) now have access to 401(k) plans.

What may come as a surprise is that a growing number of rich Americans seem to be ditching their 401(k)s, at least partly.

Craig Copeland, director of Wealth Benefits Research at the Employee Benefit Research Institute, first noticed this trend around two years ago (2), telling Bloomberg that it's only accelerated in the past 12 months. Other retirement experts and financial advisors indicated they'd seen the same phenomenon.

According to Bloomberg, although wealthy Americans often have plenty of money to hit the 401(k) contribution limit, which is $24,500 for those under 50 in 2026 (3) (and higher for older Americans eligible for catch-up contributions), high-earning investors are increasingly putting only enough into these accounts to max out their employer match.

What are they doing with their money instead? They're diverting the rest of the extra cash to other investments. In many cases, the money is going into Health Savings Accounts, Roth IRAs or even taxable brokerage accounts.

Several factors are driving this shift, but one of the most notable is the tax rate. Traditional 401(k) plans provide up-front tax savings, giving investors the chance to make pre-tax contributions. However, taking required minimum distributions is mandatory in retirement, and those withdrawals are taxable when money comes out.

Many savvy investors are wary of claiming their tax savings now, at a time when tax rates are relatively low, and then being forced to take out money at a later time, when rates could be much higher.

This is particularly the case considering the top marginal tax rate currently sits at 37% (4) — compared to 70% in 1978 (5), when Congress created the framework for 401(k) plans — which means the tax benefits these accounts provide are nowhere near as generous as they used to be.

articles.title: Weight-loss drugs are hitting alcohol a lot harder than snacks, food-and-beverage VC explains
articles.summary: Weight-loss drugs may do more damage to booze than to the snack aisle, according to Nate Cooper, founder and managing partner of Barrel Ventures.
articles.body:
Weight-loss drugs may do more damage to booze shops than to the snack aisle, according to Nate Cooper, founder and managing partner of Barrel Ventures.

"At the end of the day, you have to eat, right? What you don't have to do is you don't have to drink alcohol," Cooper, whose first real check as an investor went into the nascent stages of Olipop, told Yahoo Finance Executive Editor Brian Sozzi on the Power Players podcast (video above). "I think GLP-1s are having a much more severe impact on alcohol consumption than they are in food."

His reasoning: GLP-1 drugs "decrease addictive behaviors."

Sozzi noted that snacking giants such as PepsiCo ( PEP ), the owner of Frito-Lay, and Campbell's ( CPB ), the maker of Goldfish and Snyder's-Lance pretzels, are pushing back on the idea that GLP-1s will hurt their businesses over the long term.

Cooper expects "a slow drip effect" on snacking instead.

"Snacking is never going to disappear," he said, but brands will pack more protein and fiber into less food "because people are eating less."

What can replace alcohol if people drink less? Cooper's fund invested in Nowadays, a hemp THC beverage, a year and a half to two years ago. Cooper said Nowadays was the No. 2-selling item last year at the country's largest liquor retailer, behind a 750 ml bottle of Tito's vodka.

The appeal, he said, is "a similar feeling of having a drink or two without the downside effect of like waking up and feeling like crap in the morning."

Cooper said it's "not out of the realm of possibility" that the category could make up 10% of alcohol sales in stores, assuming it stays legal.

Extrapolated across US alcohol sales, he said, that would be $50 billion a year, for a category "that didn't exist five years ago."

He suggested a three-tier framework for lawmakers looking to regulate the drinks like alcohol: age-gate them, cap the milligrams, and "eliminate the synthetics."

articles.title: UPI vs credit cards: What should you choose for payments after MDR?
articles.summary: The author is CEO of Paisabazaar When it comes to choosing between UPI and credit cards, consumers should look at the overall value that they can derive
articles.body: The author is CEO of PaisabazaarWhen it comes to choosing between UPI and credit cards, consumers should look at the overall value that they can derive from each payment method rather than the immediate cost of the transaction. While UPI provides convenience and simplicity, credit cards offer cashback, rewards and additional perks. With MDR on higher-value UPI transactions now being discussed, understanding the complete economics of a transaction becomes even more important.The overall value of a transaction depends on several factors including the payment mode, transaction value, the applicable MDR (if any), and the value-back attached to the payment method. This becomes particularly relevant as UPI increasingly intersects with the credit card ecosystem through RuPay credit cards.UPI and cards serve different purposes in the consumer walletWhen a consumer makes a UPI payment from a bank account, the money is deducted directly from the account. While this offers simplicity and convenience, such payments generally do not come with any meaningful rewards, apart from occasional merchant-specific offers.A credit card changes this equation. The consumer can make the purchase today and get an interest-free period of 40-50 days, depending on the card's billing cycle and payment terms. Moreover, when it is a RuPay Credit Card that supports UPI payments, this flexibility is combined with the convenience of UPI.Value-back as rewards or cashback can change the economicsCredit cards are increasingly being designed around specific spending behaviours. Depending on the card, consumers can earn cashback or reward points on categories ranging from everyday purchases to high-ticket spends like travel bookings and electronics.Consider a Rs. 50,000 transaction on a card offering 5% cashback on the spend. The consumer could potentially receive Rs 2,500 back, subject to the card's terms, redemption value and applicable caps. Now if the consumer chooses to pay the same amount through UPI and the merchant passes on the entire MDR cost of 0.4% to the consumer, they will end up paying an additional Rs 200, making the product costlier for them, with no additional benefits.In fact, in most scenarios, credit cards can offer greater value to consumers through rewards, cashback and other benefits, without any additional payment processing charges being levied on them. However, this holds true only if consumers pay their credit card bills in full and on time, avoiding interest or finance charges. Once interest starts accruing on outstanding balances, it can outweigh the value earned through rewards or cashback, potentially nullifying the benefits of using a credit card.This is why comparing payment methods purely on the basis of transaction charges like MDR could be misleading. Rewards, offers and other value-back systems should also be taken into account. At the same time, a card may carry an annual or joining fee, impose reward caps, exclude certain categories, or offer a lower reward rate on certain transactions – which should also be considered.Transaction size alone does not determine the better choiceA common assumption is that UPI is best suited to small purchases while cards make more sense for larger transactions. However, in practice, the answer is more nuanced.Even a small Rs 500 transaction on a credit card could be more valuable than the same transaction through bank-account UPI if the card offers meaningful cashback or rewards on that particular spend. Conversely, a Rs 50,000 transaction may not necessarily justify the use of a credit card if the transaction falls outside the card's reward categories or has already exhausted the applicable monthly reward cap.Consumers should, therefore, look at the frequency of spending and the cumulative rewards generated over time. Small individual transactions can add up to significant value when they form a large portion of monthly expenditure. At the same time, card-specific discounts, cashback, merchant offers and reward points may add further value. Hence, the effective benefit can vary considerably across cards and merchants, irrespective of transaction values.Credit cards can offer value beyond the immediate transactionAn often-overlooked aspect of credit card payments is that their value is not limited to rewards. For consumers who manage their credit responsibly, the interest-free period can provide useful cash-flow flexibility. Some transactions may also be eligible for EMI conversion, allowing a large purchase to be spread across several months. Credit cards also come with issuer-specific offers, milestone benefits, travel privileges and more.But these benefits only have value when they are actually relevant to the consumer. Paying an annual fee for benefits that are rarely used does not necessarily make economic sense.The consumer's spending pattern should drive the choiceUltimately, there is no single payment method that will offer the best value for every consumer or every transaction. The important shift is to stop looking at payment methods only through the lens of convenience or transaction value and instead consider the net economics of the payment and choose the payment instrument that delivers the most meaningful value for one's individual spending pattern.MDR may change the equation, but not necessarily in the same way for everyoneThe discussion around MDR on higher-value UPI transactions adds another dimension to this comparison. MDR represents a cost associated with accepting a digital payment, and the relative economics for merchants can vary across payment instruments and transaction types.The impact on consumers, however, will depend on how the ecosystem responds. If merchants absorb the additional cost, there may be little or no visible impact on the consumer. If the cost is reflected in pricing or an additional payment-related charge, consumers may have to pay it as part of the product’s cost.Whether and to what extent merchants pass such costs on to consumers is yet to be seen.(Disclaimer: Recommendations and views on the stock market, or any other asset classes or personal finance management tips given by experts and analysts are their own. These opinions do not represent the views of The Times of India.)You use AI every day. Now get your AI Quotient. Take the AIQ test.

articles.title: Who would buy a home at today's mortgage rates?
articles.summary: Just 6% of homeowners and renters would take out a mortgage at today's rates.
articles.body:
Who wants to buy a home when mortgage rates are above 7%? The answer, unsurprisingly, is not many people.

The housing consulting firm John Burns Research & Consulting surveyed homeowners and renters about the highest rate they would accept on a mortgage. Just 6% said they would be willing to pay 7.5% to 7.99%, around today's current levels.

But if rates fell below 5.5%, nearly half of those surveyed would be willing to take out a mortgage. That level is something of a "magic mortgage rate" that market watchers believe would unleash a surge of new demand and bring sales out of their low-gear state. While rates never hit 5.5% this year, mortgage applications did pick up noticeably when rates were hovering around 6% earlier this year. And the latest rate rise has had a strong chilling effect on the market. Zillow found that pending home sales, which are recorded when a home goes under contract, were down 8.5% in September compared to a year earlier.

Claire Boston is a senior reporter for Yahoo Finance covering housing, mortgages, and home insurance.

articles.title: Trump launches new effort to oust Fed Governor Lisa Cook
articles.summary: President Donald Trump is mounting a fresh offensive in his battle to oust Federal Reserve Governor Lisa Cook, forming a committee of his own appointees to investigate allegations against her.
articles.body: President Donald Trump is mounting a fresh offensive in his battle to oust Federal Reserve Governor Lisa Cook, forming a committee of his own appointees to investigate allegations against her. The committee will investigate alleged false statements Cook made in connection with mortgages on two properties and hold an in-person hearing at the White House on November 5, the White House announced on Friday. Analysts say the formation of the committee and setting of a hearing date indicate Trump officials are addressing procedural issues addressed by a June Supreme Court ruling that initially blocked the administration from removing Cook. Newly installed Labor Secretary Keith Sonderling, who is also serving as acting director of the Office of Government Ethics, is one of the three members. So is National Economic Council Director Kevin Hassett, a staunch defender of Trump’s economic agenda, whom the president considered for Fed chair. The third member is Andrea Lucas, chair of the Equal Employment Opportunity Commission. Cook’s attorneys, Abbe Lowell and Norm Eisen, said they have been in touch with the White House “to evaluate whether the process proposed has a possibility of being a genuine one and not simply a box-checking exercise.” “Governor Cook welcomes the opportunity to present the facts so she can clear her name and demonstrate there is no legal basis to fire her,” they said in a statement provided to CNN on Friday. The formation of the committee marks the latest salvo in Trump’s ongoing attempts to reshape the Fed and comes just weeks ahead of its next monetary policy meeting, where officials will consider whether interest rate changes are merited. “This seems tailor-made to address the Supreme Court’s biggest criticism in its last attempt: that Governor Cook didn’t have a chance to defend herself,” said Tim Mahedy, a former official at the Federal Reserve Bank of San Francisco, who is now CEO of research firm Access/Macro. Mahedy said the outcome of this review “is clear” given the makeup of the committee. He expressed surprise that Hassett, a White House economist, would be on a committee investigating a legal matter about paperwork. Trump has long berated the politically independent Fed because it hasn’t lowered interest rates to his liking, publicly targeting Cook and former Fed Chair Jerome Powell. But Trump has spared the current chairman, Kevin Warsh, whom he appointed to the position earlier this year after Powell’s term at the head of the central bank expired. Instead, Trump has insisted that Warsh is blocked by a “political” Board of Governors. The central bank’s eight-member Board votes on interest rate decisions, along with regional Fed presidents. While the Fed leader often plays an influential role in shaping the discussion on policy moves, decisions are ultimately the result of the 12-person committee process. At its September meeting, all 12 members, including Warsh, voted to raise rates for the first time in three years in an effort to contain inflation that has heated up largely due to the US war with Iran. Trump said later that Warsh shouldn’t have greenlit a rate hike. “I don’t blame Kevin Warsh. I probably would have voted against the Board if I were him,” Trump said in an interview Time Magazine published earlier this month. Separately, Trump reaffirmed he wants Warsh to “vote the way he wants.” Trump vs. Cook Trump previously sought to fire Cook over unproven allegations of mortgage fraud. Ultimately, in a 5-4 decision earlier this year, the Supreme Court ruled Trump could not immediately remove her. “The 5-4 Supreme Court decision did not prohibit President Trump from firing a Fed Governor, it gave him a roadmap to do it,” Ed Mills, Washington policy analyst at Raymond James, told CNN in an email. Chief Justice John Roberts wrote in his majority opinion released in June that Cook was entitled to sufficient time and notice to respond to a termination and that she wasn’t given a fair opportunity to respond last year when Trump initially sought to remove her. But that doesn’t mean Trump can’t lawfully fire her, he said. The law allows a president to remove Fed governors “for cause,” which is generally interpreted to mean negligence or malfeasance in the role. The “ultimate question of whether the presi­dent can remove Cook for cause will depend in part on the underlying facts,” Roberts wrote. “We have not addressed the facts, as they have yet to be found or analyzed under the relevant legal standards.” Mills said Cook is “very clearly at risk of being fired, and it is unclear if the Supreme Court would block President Trump in Round 2.” He added that two of Cook’s colleagues, Powell and Governor Michael Barr, are also on the list for “potential ‘for-cause’ firing.” Kurt Lewis, a former special adviser to Powell who is now head of central bank policy at Piper Sandler, said this will ultimately come down to how much deference the Supreme Court gives the president on “cause” once justices think he has “followed a semblance of procedure.” Cook was appointed by former President Joe Biden in 2022 and is the first Black female Fed governor, with a term set to expire in 2038. This story has been updated with additional content.

articles.title: Video game hardware sales plunge to 13-year low as prices soar on memory, storage shortage
articles.summary: Video game console sales have plunged 13% on the memory and storage crisis.
articles.body:
The video game industry is taking a serious beating from the global memory and storage shortage. Microsoft ( MSFT ), Nintendo ( NTDOY ), and Sony ( SONY ) have all raised the prices on their respective consoles to offset both the increased component costs and the prior impact of tariffs.

And that has sent sales plummeting. According to data from market research group Circana, video game hardware sales for August fell 15% year over year to their lowest August totals in 13 years.

Take Sony's PlayStation 5, for example. A version of the console without a disc drive launched at $399 in November 2020. Today, it will cost you $599 . A version with a disc drive launched at $499 and now costs $649 . The high-powered PlayStation 5 Pro, which cost $699 when it debuted in 2024, is now priced at an eye-watering $899 .

Microsoft has made similar moves for its Xbox Series S and Series X. The S, which originally cost $299, is now $499, while the Series X climbed $250 to $749 .

Nintendo raised the price of the Switch 2 from $449 to $499 following President Trump's "Liberation Day" tariff increases last year.

According to Circana, video game hardware spending fell 3% in August, while year-to-date spending is down 11%.

"We are seeing the negative impact of those higher price points on the consoles. We're seeing a reduction in unit sales, driven by those higher prices," Circana executive director of games Mat Piscatella explained.

"We're also starting to see, spotty right now, but we're starting to see some products becoming unavailable, likely because of the RAM and component crisis," he added.

According to Piscatella, Sony's PlayStation 5 Pro, in particular, is extremely hard to find, with some retailers selling used versions of the console for more than $1,000, though it's unclear if that's directly related to the memory and storage shortage.

The big question, for Sony and Microsoft at least, is what all of this means for the launch of Take-Two Interactive's upcoming "Grand Theft Auto VI." One of the most anticipated media launches in history, "GTA VI" is expected to boost console sales among consumers who have held off on purchasing systems to date.

But higher prices could give some would-be buyers pause.

"The laggards of entering this generation, I bet a bunch of them are assuming that they're going to go to the store and pick [up a console] for $200, and instead it's going to be $600, $700, $800, $900 to try to pick up a console to play the thing," Piscatella said.

"I think there's going to be some sticker shock there if the consoles are even on the shelf to begin with," he said. "I'm sure there's going to be some kind of moderate [sales] boost, but there are so many factors at play."

articles.body:
So much for the SaaSpocalypse eating all software stocks alive until they hit $0.

The overused 2026 market slang — which promoted the view that AI players like Anthropic ( ANTH.PVT ) and OpenAI ( OPAI.PVT ) would crush the business models of software-as-a-service companies — should be put to bed. Because after a stretch where this narrative hammered many software players, most have rallied sharply back.

The broader software group and the IGV index have rallied significantly since the end of June, JPMorgan strategist Samik Chatterjee pointed out (see the chart below), up 21% since the end of the month relative to the broader S&P 500 ( ^GSPC ), up 4%. Some of the top performers include Paycom ( PAYC ), DocuSign ( DOCU ), Workday ( WDAY ), Salesforce ( CRM ), Cloudflare ( NET ), Twilio ( TWLO ), and Microsoft ( MSFT ).

The broader rally has, in part, been helped by a valuation multiple rerating across infrastructure and application software companies, Chatterjee noted.

Renewed belief in software stocks could be sustained into year-end as investors digest third quarter earnings reports.

"Heading into C3Q earnings, we expect the broader share price momentum for the group to continue with infrastructure software companies leading the way on account of the AI-led tailwinds driving robust beats on both top-line and earnings, albeit potentially only in line on gross margins," Chatterjee said.

He added, "We expect application software companies to also participate in the positive share price momentum for the sector into the year-end on account of raises to full-year guides, aided by building momentum in AI monetization, which is steadily building as incremental revenue on top of the core businesses, which range from modestly decelerating to stable growth across our coverage companies."

articles.title: She worked as a teacher till 62 years of age instead of retiring at 60, but was denied gratuity because of extended service; Allahabad HC orders payment with 6% interest
articles.summary: You work several years in an educational institution and are denied gratuity on the grounds that you worked beyond the retirement age. What do you do?
articles.body: You work several years in an educational institution and are denied gratuity on the grounds that you worked beyond the retirement age. What do you do? In one such case a retired teacher was denied gratuity and she challenged it in court.What the case is aboutA woman joined an educational institution in Faizabad as an assistant teacher on August 16, 1992. She continued working there until March 31, 2019, when she retired. However, the institution declined to pay her gratuity, arguing that the prescribed retirement age was 60 and she had remained in service until she was 62.On September 13, 2023, the Principal Secretary of the Uttar Pradesh Government's Minority Welfare Department rejected her claim for gratuity. The decision was based solely on the fact that she had continued working beyond the age of 60 and retired at 62.Also Read | Sisters sought share in parents’ properties under Hindu Succession law; Madras HC rules for brother over mother’s land on ouster, father’s estate over missing partiesThe retired teacher challenged the decision in court, arguing that working beyond the prescribed retirement age should not deprive her of gratuity. She pointed out that she had served the institution continuously for several years before retiring on March 31, 2019.Her challenge succeeded on September 30, 2026, when the Allahabad High Court directed the educational institution to pay her outstanding gratuity immediately, along with interest at 6% from 2019.Why did the retired teacher win the gratuity case?The Allahabad High Court noted that the state-regulated madrasa had refused to pay the woman’s gratuity by relying on government orders and rules, according to an ET report. According to the institution, she had failed to exercise her option to receive gratuity within the stipulated period.However, the court pointed out that she had been allowed to continue working until the age of 62 and had received all other retirement benefits admissible to her.The Allahabad High Court observed that merely citing the applicable government orders and alleging that the employee had not exercised the required option was insufficient to settle the question of her gratuity entitlement.Also Read | Retired bank employee got Rs 12.27 lakh leave encashment and claimed Rs 3 lakh exemption in 2020, but government later hiked limit to Rs 25 lakh in 2023; ITAT Chennai allows full tax exemptionThis was particularly relevant because the issue of denying gratuity on the basis of such an option had subsequently been examined authoritatively by both the Allahabad High Court and the Supreme Court, the report said.The court said that once the legal implications of allowing an employee to remain in service beyond the prescribed retirement age had been examined, and it had been held that such an extension could not, in the circumstances considered, justify denial of gratuity, the institution was required to assess the retired teacher’s claim in accordance with that legal position.The Allahabad High Court also referred to a Supreme Court judgment recognising gratuity as a beneficial scheme intended to protect eligible employees, reinforcing the principle that the benefit should be paid to those entitled to receive it.The Allahabad High Court observed that the teacher had been permitted to remain in service until March 31, 2019, when she turned 62, and had continued working accordingly. While settling her retirement benefits, the institution could not disregard the legal consequences arising from her extended service.Also Read | US-based daughter files case against parents seeking share in properties; Karnataka HC rejects her ‘ancestral’ claim, saying they were father's separate assets, not coparcenary propertyThe court further noted that the order rejecting her gratuity claim did not show that the institution had independently examined her entitlement to the benefit. Instead, the rejection rested on the allegation that she had not exercised the option to retire at the age of 60.Advocate Mayank Parashar of law firm Clasis Law explained to ET that Indian labour laws have traditionally placed employees' social security interests at the centre.Under both the new Labour Codes and the earlier legal framework, the circumstances in which gratuity can be denied are restricted. Continuing in employment beyond the retirement age with the employer's permission does not, by itself, constitute a valid ground for disqualification.According to Parashar, the retired woman succeeded because the reason cited for withholding her gratuity was not recognised as a legally valid ground under the applicable law.Although the judgment concerned an employee of a madrasa operating under state regulation, Parashar said its significance extends to establishments more broadly, including private-sector employers. The ruling underscores the need to assess gratuity claims properly before making a decision.Employers must have a clear and legally defensible reason before withholding or refusing gratuity or any other social security benefit, he added.The Allahabad High Court ruled in the retired teacher’s favour, entitling her to receive the outstanding gratuity along with interest at 6%.You use AI every day. articles.title: 128-year-old iconic furniture chain closing down and liquidating all locations
articles.summary: The furniture chain, which opened in 1898, will discontinue its two retail store brands.
articles.body:
The furniture retail sector has been downsizing in 2026 as several retailers have permanently closed their doors for good.

Certain furniture chains have lined up to close their establishments in the days and months ahead, with some setting firm dates to shutter, while others are not so certain.

Family-owned and operated Pieroway's Furniture chain announced that it will close its doors for the final time on Oct. 31, as the company's owner plans to retire and shut down the business. The 60-year-old furniture retailer said it will close its stores in Ludlow and West Springfield, Mass., following month-long liquidation sales, according to a Oct. 1 company statement.

107-year-old retail store Weiss Furniture in Latrobe, Pa., said it would close permanently following a liquidation sale that began Sept. 3, the shop's owner said in a statement.

Haynes Furniture plans liquidation sales

And now, the 128-year-old family-owned and operated Haynes Furniture chain has launched a going-out-of-business sale on Oct. 8, 2026, with plans to permanently close its four Virginia retail stores, as well as its eight The Dump Luxe Furniture luxury brand outlets in five states, the company said in a statement.

The company has not announced its last day of operations yet.

The furniture retailer had already announced in September that it would close six of its The Dump Luxe Furniture locations in Texas, Illinois, Arizona, and Georgia.

"This is a bittersweet ending, filled with gratitude for four generations of customers and employees," Haynes Executive Chairman E.J. Strelitz said in the statement. "Thank you to everyone who helped us along the way."

Haynes Furniture has hired turnaround, restructuring, and asset disposition advisory firm SB360 Capital Partners to assist in its going-out-of-business sale. The company has not filed for bankruptcy at last check.

The retailer also has not revealed the number of employees who will be affected by the closings.

Haynes Furniture did not give specific reasons for closing down its 12 stores, but Strelitz said he was planning a "well-deserved retirement."

Strelitz represents the third generation of his family to operate the furniture chain after his grandparents, Ellia and Minnie, purchased a small furniture store in Norfolk, Va., in 1930 that had operated for over 30 years, Home News Now reported. The legacy passed on to the next generation of Leonard and Buddy Strelitz with Tom Hofheimer before E.J. Strelitz took over the business.

articles.title: The bull market in stocks is about to enter its fifth year — here's what the data says is next
articles.summary: Break out the birthday balloons for the bull market.
articles.body:
Break out the birthday balloons for the bull market .

Investors are currently living in the 11th bull market since the 1950s, which is on track to become the seventh to complete at least four full years on Oct. 12, according to a new analysis by Truist co-chief investment officer Keith Lerner.

Measured against every bull market dating back to the 1950s, the 119% advance sits near the middle of the pack, well below the 401% gain during the 2009-2020 cycle and the 582% gain from 1987-2000.

The historical average advance for a bull market in Lerner's measurement period is 184%. Of the 10 prior bull markets, six lasted longer than four years.

Among bull markets that reached this stage, the fifth year produced an average return of 12% and a median return of 15%.

"The weight of the evidence remains supportive as the bull market enters its fifth year," Lerner wrote. "Continued economic growth, resilient corporate profits, and a meaningful reset in valuations provide a solid foundation for maintaining a constructive stance. At the same time, history suggests investors should not get caught off guard by volatility as the cycle matures."

The bull market this year has been powered by the one-two punch of strong corporate earnings and AI optimism.

articles.title: ‘Zero tolerance for disruptions.’ Hurricane Isaias could mess with America’s refining nerve center
articles.summary: Hurricane Isaias is barreling down on the US Gulf Coast at a time when there’s almost no margin for error in the global energy system.
articles.body: Hurricane Isaias is barreling down on the US Gulf Coast at a time when there’s almost no margin for error in the global energy system. The biggest risk is that extreme flooding, wind or power outages from the Category 3 storm disrupts, damages or even destroys refineries. The world is already relying on US refineries to process as much oil as possible to make up for a fuel supply crunch caused by war in the Middle East and Russia. Analysts warn that even a small disruption could cause a big price hike in gas, diesel and jet fuel. “There is zero tolerance for any disruptions right now,” said Tom Kloza, chief energy adviser at Gulf Oil. “If we lose a refinery — even just for a few weeks — it can manifest itself in very high prices very quickly.” Beyond the danger to vital refineries, the storm has temporarily knocked offline almost two-thirds of the oil production in the Gulf of Mexico. And there is a risk that Hurricane Isaias delays crucial fuel deliveries to Florida. The good news, relatively speaking, is that the path of the storm has veered far enough to the east that it could spare most, though not all, Gulf Coast refiners. Refineries in Louisiana are expected to avoid the worst of the storm. Given the current path of the storm, Lipow said he’s “less concerned” about the risk to the overall system than a few days ago. Mississippi, Alabama refineries in focus Still, Lipow says two major refineries are at significant risk from the storm: the Chevron facility in Pascagoula, Mississippi, and the Vertex facility in Mobile, Alabama. Together, they process a combined 466,000 barrels per day, representing about 2.4% of the nation’s refining capacity, according to Lipow. “Hurricane Isaias is a fuel supply event hitting a system already stretched by the Iran war,” analysts at Jefferies said in a report. “A small disruption now has outsized price consequences.” The big question is whether extreme flooding or power outages in the region force the Chevron and Vertex refineries to shut down for a significant amount of time. Lipow notes that it can take up to two weeks to fully restart refineries even if they avoid damage. “Severe flooding can put a refinery out of commission for months,” Lipow said. Hurricane Ida in 2021 caused significant damage to refineries, forcing multiple shutdowns. That Category 4 storm unleashed such extreme flooding that Phillips 66 eventually pulled the plug on its Alliance Refinery in Belle Chasse, Louisiana. Repairs were so costly that the company opted to convert the facility to a terminal. Kloza, the Gulf Oil executive, said he suspects both the Chevron and Vertex refineries will avoid catastrophic damage. “I don’t think the hurricane is going to knock out these two refineries. But you do have to worry about the utilities. If you don’t have power, you can’t operate. That’s the biggest threat,” Kloza said. Last month, an ExxonMobil refinery in Joliet, Illinois, experienced power problems that forced the facility to go offline. Gasoline and diesel prices skyrocketed, underscoring the low margin for error in the system. If any refinery shuts down from the hurricane, it will force suppliers to withdraw more fuel from already-thin stockpiles, which act as shock absorbers during crises. Commercial inventories of both gasoline and diesel are historically low for this time of year because of the fuel supply crunch caused by overseas outages in China, the Middle East and Russia. Stockpiles of diesel, the workhorse fuel that powers the modern economy, are at the lowest seasonal level since federal data started in 1982. 63% of Gulf oil output sidelined Hurricane Isaias has already disrupted oil production in the Gulf of Mexico. As of midday on Friday, oil companies shut in about 72% of the daily Gulf of Mexico oil production as a precaution. Assuming there is no damage, those facilities should be able to resume production in short order. Another potential issue is getting gasoline and fuel to Florida, a state that is reliant on shipments from Gulf Coast refineries because it lacks any major refineries of its own. Lipow said there will likely be some “slight” delays getting fuel to Florida because tankers must wait for the storm to pass before crossing the Gulf of Mexico.

Two Cash App settlements are drawing interest from users: One settlement is currently being paid, and the other has recently issued payments. Claims can no longer be filed for either one.

Cash App and its parent company, Block Inc. ( XYZ ), are issuing payments in October as part of a settlement of a class action lawsuit over alleged security breaches that occurred between Aug. 23, 2018, and Aug. 20, 2024. The deadline to file a claim has passed.

The $15 million settlement fund pays previously approved claimants up to $2,500 for out-of-pocket losses, transaction losses, and up to $75 for three hours of lost time.

The other settlement, totaling $175 million, involved a consent order in which the Consumer Financial Protection Bureau accused Cash App of failing to protect users from fraud. Details on that June payout are below.

The lawsuit alleged that a former Cash App employee and an unauthorized person used recycled phone numbers to gain access to accounts. The plaintiffs also claimed that a security breach exposed personal information of Cash App Investing customers. The class action lawsuit alleged that the company failed to respond effectively to complaints about payment issues and that users found it difficult to obtain assistance from Cash App support.

The company pledged to improve data security but denied any fault or wrongdoing.

The deadline to file a claim was Nov. 18, 2024, and a California court gave final approval to the settlement in March 2025. Approved claimants are expected to receive payments this month by check, prepaid card, Venmo, or Zelle.

About 40,380 claims were approved out of over 667,000 filed, totaling $5.6 million and averaging approximately $139 per payout, before any adjustments.

A separate CFPB settlement has already been paid

Cash App users who qualified for the settlement checks were sent an email with the subject line "Your Compensation Payment from Cash App is on the Way."

No claim form was required for this settlement. Cash App's parent company, Block Inc. identified eligible customers. Checks were mailed beginning June 8 by Epiq Global, a third-party settlement administrator. The amounts issued varied by customer and weren't publicly released.

For questions related to this settlement, call 888-832-1301 between 8:30 a.m. and 9:00 p.m. ET.

A third settlement, a $12.5 million case over Cash App referral texts, was paid to Washington state residents in April 2026.

Any offer to file a late claim or offer a Cash App payment for a fee in any settlement is likely a scam.

President Trump teased an upcoming announcement Friday from Office of Management and Budget Director Russell Vought as well as one pertaining to diesel.

“We have a big announcement coming up on diesel,” Trump said, speaking at a Columbus Day celebration in the White House East Room.

Trump also said Vought would be making a “tremendous announcement” in the near future.

“He’ll be even more important than Chris if he pulls this off,” the president quipped, referring to Energy Secretary Chris Wright. “He’s working on something that’s going to be so good for our country.”

On Wednesday, Trump had hinted at a forthcoming announcement from his budget director.

“We have some big surprises coming up in another few weeks, right, Russ?” Trump said, speaking at an event in Baltimore. “He’s going to be one of the very important people in the history of our country, in my opinion. He’s got some great things happening.”

The teases come as Trump has been rolling out a number of new announcements ahead of the midterms, including initiatives focused on energy affordability as voters continue to struggle with costs.

Trump signed an executive order Monday during a rally in Nebraska, home to a competitive Senate race, that seeks to increase the availability of red-dyed diesel . Last week, Trump announced the South Korean government will invest up to $200 billion in U.S. energy infrastructure, including a natural gas pipeline in Alaska.

articles.title: Elon Musk’s growing SpaceX empire sends AT&T, Verizon and T-Mobile shares plunging
articles.summary: Elon Musk’s plan for SpaceX to become a major mobile carrier sent shares of AT&T, Verizon and T-Mobile plunging and wiped out over $50 billion before lunch.
articles.body: Elon Musk’s plan for SpaceX to “become a major mobile carrier in the U.S.” sent shares of the nation’s big three wireless carriers sliding by double digits Friday, wiping out more than $50 billion in market value before lunch. “Once we receive final FCC approval, Starlink Mobile will deploy a flexible architecture combining our satellite-to-mobile constellation in space with an advanced terrestrial deployment that can seamlessly connect devices everywhere,” the company said late Thursday. It also announced that the Federal Communications Commission had approved the launch of 15,000 new satellites, also under Starlink Mobile, which is a subsidiary of SpaceX. Shares of AT&T fell 9.8%, Verizon dropped 8.7%, while T-Mobile US plunged 13.3%. For Verizon, today’s performance was its worst-one day drop since 2002. It was T-Mobile’s worst day since 2011. Shares of Charter and of Comcast, the parent company of NBC News, also fell Friday. Both companies sell wireless services under their own brands using Verizon’s infrastructure. Musk’s empire expands The announcement from SpaceX marked Musk’s latest step to expand his global tech empire. The world’s richest man and its first-ever trillionaire, Musk’s net worth as of Thursday was about $990 billion. Musk’s constellation of companies already includes electric vehicle maker Tesla, the social media site X and xAI, which builds data centers and develops artificial intelligence. SpaceX includes multiple lines of business, too. Starlink sells high-speed internet to companies and consumers worldwide, while Starshield does the same, but to governments. But the major money maker for SpaceX is Starlink, which was worth $2.2 trillion as of Friday. With more than 12 million paying subscribers, Starlink is also the only profitable part of SpaceX’s business, according to its latest earnings report. The acquisition of spectrum was “the last critical piece of the spectrum puzzle needed for SpaceX to provide complete phone coverage in America,” Musk wrote on n X. SpaceX is also a massive U.S. government contractor, building and launching rockets on behalf of NASA and several national security agencies. Favorable decisions by government regulators and additional agency contracts are crucial to maintaining SpaceX’s lofty valuation. White House VIP As a close ally of President Donald Trump and a major donor to his 2024 election effort, Musk is a frequent guest at White House events. At a recent White House state dinner for China’s President Xi Jinping, Musk was seated next to first lady Melania Trump. Just this week, Trump gave Musk an award for achievements in science. As Republicans struggle to hold on to control of the House and Senate in November’s midterm elections, Musk is once again giving tens of millions of dollars to help them. As of Friday, Musk’s America PAC had spent more than $36 million to boost Trump’s fellow Republicans in key battleground races, according to figures compiled by Wired and verified by NBC News. Musk also appears to have support for his deal already from FCC chairman Brendan Carr. “All of this is going to be really good news for the American consumer,” Carr said Friday morning on CNBC. Skeptics on the street Wall Street analysts and Starlink’s potential competitors were skeptical Friday of the SpaceX plan. Absent a deal with an existing wireless carrier, “SpaceX would likely need to build a terrestrial network using macro towers to deliver a user experience on par with traditional wireless carriers,” wrote analysts at JPMorgan Chase. “We continue to see limited near-term risk to U.S. wireless incumbents given the time, infrastructure and capital required to build a competitive terrestrial network,” they added. Put another way, the analysts think SpaceX plan’s does not pose an imminent threat to the established carriers because it takes a lot more than just satellites to deliver reliable wireless service. SpaceX would need earth-based infrastructure to bolster its network of satellites because the radio waves it purchased would likely be unable to reach the interior of some buildings, wrote analysts at UBS. “We still believe it will take time for SpaceX to scale its wireless ambitions.” Like the analysts, the major telecom companies feeling the sting from Musk’s announcement also downplayed any risk that Starlink might pose to their businesses. “Acquisition of spectrum alone does not provide the network or infrastructure to offer true nationwide coverage or to compete with mobile providers,” Verizon said in a statement to NBC News. “A company can have billions of dollars of spectrum, but if they do not have the network to use it, it’s just empty airwaves.” John Saw, president of technology at T-Mobile wrote, “I have tremendous respect for what SpaceX has accomplished in space,” but that building a network would take “years of engineering.” “You can acquire spectrum in a single transaction. You cannot acquire a nationwide, high-performing wireless network overnight,” he wrote on LinkedIn. AT&T did not respond to a request for comment on Friday. The three big wireless companies have a complicated relationship with Starlink. In 2022, T-Mobile announced a partnership with SpaceX, but recently dropped the name of the company from parts of its website. And when the three wireless companies announced a joint venture recently to “eliminate coverage ‘dead zones’ and expand satellite coverage,” there was no mention of SpaceX or Starlink.

articles.title: PERM freeze: Indian IT stocks rally, but talent exodus looms
articles.summary: US suspends PERM processing for some Indian IT firms; stocks rally but H-1B talent may exit to protect green card paths, raising retention risks.
articles.body: BENGALURU/HUDERABAD: Even as the US govt suspended processing under the Permanent Labour Certification (PERM) programme for some Indian IT firms, potentially jeopardising eligible employees’ pathways to permanent residency, the sector’s stocks rallied on Friday, suggesting limited market concern amid declining dependence on H-1B visas.However, the suspension could create talent retention and hiring challenges. H-1B employees may move to employers not covered by the suspension to keep their green card applications on track, potentially triggering an exodus of skilled professionals. Top talent may also hesitate to join affected companies if doing so means losing a viable pathway to permanent residency.Vikram Shroff, partner for employment, labour and benefits at AZB & Partners, said the suspension should not affect Indian IT companies’ ability to service US clients, although it could delay new applications. “It is hoped that the suspension is temporary and is withdrawn once the investigation is completed,” he said.TCS said the PERM programme suspension was unlikely to affect its workforce strategy or customer engagements, as its applications under the programme had been in single digits over the past two years.“Our original business model has always been that people go from here, work on the project, go onsite, spend two, three years there, and come back. So there is a continuous movement of talent between onsite and offshore,” TCS CEO K Krithivasan said.As of October last year, TCS had around 11,000 H-1B employees in its 32,000-33,000-strong US workforce. While acknowledging that some employees may want to stay in the US permanently, Krithivasan said permanent residency had never been central to the company’s workforce strategy. Local employees account for 50% of TCS’s US workforce, and the company plans to hire another 15,000 people there over five years.Microsoft said 80% of the approximately 6,000 H-1B visa applications it filed in the last fiscal year were to extend or change the status of existing employees. Applications for new hires accounted for just 1% of its US workforce and involved individuals already legally present in the country.“We pay our employees some of the highest compensation in the tech sector, and our wages are among the highest of all H-1B filings. We pay our H-1B employees the same as any other employees doing comparable work,” the company said in a statement.Cyrus D Mehta, managing partner of New York-based law firm Cyrus D Mehta & Partners, called the suspension a “warped approach”. “Immigration is not a zero-sum game,” he said, disputing the suggestion that hiring foreign workers necessarily takes jobs away from Americans. Responding to Vice-President JD Vance’s criticism of Microsoft over its 2025 layoffs, Mehta said the layoffs did not prevent companies from recruiting foreign workers with specialised skills.Stephen Yale-Loehr, a retired professor of immigration law practice at Cornell Law School, called the Department of Labor’s action illegal, arguing that companies had not been given a due process hearing before their applications were suspended.“I am sure the companies will sue. But litigation takes time, and in the meantime these companies can’t use the PERM green card system. This is another attack on legal immigration by the Trump administration,” he said.David J Bier, director of immigration studies at the Cato Institute, said he viewed the current US administration as the most hostile to legal immigration of any administration.Industry leaders said the suspension affecting eight major technology companies could accelerate the shift of high-value technology work to India and boost growth in global capability centres (GCCs), despite a limited immediate impact.Former HCL Technologies CEO Vineet Nayar said Indian IT companies accounted for fewer than 1,400 of the 117,849 PERM certifications issued last year, suggesting the direct impact could be limited. He said the move could accelerate the relocation of US technology work to India.Former Tech Mahindra CEO CP Gurnani and co-founder and vice-chairman of AIONOS, said India should use the opportunity to attract experienced technology talent back home.Nasscom senior vice-president and chief strategy officer Sangeeta Gupta said the business impact was likely to be negligible, as companies had filed few PERM applications in recent years and the move was prospective, not retrospective.You use AI every day. articles.title: Iran Protects Capacity to Build Missiles as Trump Pauses Strikes
articles.summary: Iran has managed to preserve its missile and drone factories despite months of US and Israeli bombing, officials familiar with the matter said, allowing it t...
articles.body:
(Bloomberg) -- Iran has managed to preserve its missile and drone factories despite months of US and Israeli bombing, officials familiar with the matter said, allowing it to replenish its arsenals while President Donald Trump holds off on strikes ahead of the midterm elections.

Tehran still has the capacity to manufacture weapons to rebuild its arsenal, according to the Western officials, who asked not to be identified discussing private assessments. One official said Iran remains well-stocked with ballistic missiles and some anti-ship weapons, and can quickly add more.

The Western official said Russia was providing missiles as well, echoing a separate assessment in June. Russia's Ministry of Defense did not respond to a request for comment.

The assessment of Iran's capability runs counter to repeated claims from Trump and his team that eight months of airstrikes have decimated Iran's ability to threaten US bases in the region and American allies. Trump said earlier this year that Iran's military is "totally destroyed" and in a speech on Sept. 30 Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth said the US had destroyed Iran's "military industrial capacity" and "their entire defense base."

That ability raises the likelihood that Iran could reconstitute its missile forces if Trump makes good on a vow, delivered via social media on Thursday, not to attack Iran before November's midterm elections. In addition, Tehran has escalated attacks on shipping around the Strait of Hormuz, hitting at least 10 vessels in the last week, according to the UK Navy.

The White House and the Pentagon didn't immediately respond to requests for comment.

Trump had earlier floated the possibility of ramping up military strikes after the elections, amid a flurry of attacks on shipping. The later time frame would allow him to avoid further fanning oil prices just before the ballot.

Assessments from Western officials signal the Islamic Republic still has enough firepower to retaliate if Washington resumes airstrikes. With its economy withering behind a US Navy blockade of its oil exports and the war stuck in limbo, Tehran may lean deeper into asymmetric warfare, seeking to inflict as much pain as possible on its much bigger opponent.
