articles.title: AI deepfake ads grow more popular in US midterm campaigns, blurring truth
articles.summary: The US midterm election campaign has been filled with political ads featuring AI deepfakes that can mislead voters.
articles.body:
San Francisco, USA: Bruce Blakeman, a Republican who is running for governor of New York, released campaign ads featuring Zohran Mamdani, New York City mayor, and Kathy Hochul, the state’s governor, gardening together and collaborating to raise prices for residents.

Another ad features Hochul talking about hiking tolls and fares so people cannot afford to drive or take the subway.

Neither Hochul nor Mamdani was actually in the ads, which were made using artificial intelligence (AI). A spate of AI-generated ads that are obviously fake but grab voter attention have been a feature of campaigns in the lead up to the pivotal United States midterm elections on November 3.

While regulation has focused on labelling AI deepfakes that could mislead voters, it is “slopaganda” – or identifiably fake ads – that mark this campaign season, says Scott Babwah Brennen, director of New York University’s Center on Technology Policy and co-author of a recent report, Political Slopaganda.

Political candidates and their supporters have spent more than $80m to make more than 164 AI-based ads this election season, according to the Wesleyan Media Project, a non-partisan election advertising tracker. Republican candidates and their backers were behind 80 percent of these ads, the group found.

Blakeman defended his ads, saying they were clearly labelled as AI-generated – a disclaimer the ads do carry for a few seconds at the start – and follow a long tradition of satire and parody in American politics.

But slopaganda – a mix of low-quality AI “slop” and propaganda – is being used to “communicate deeper truths rather than factual truths”, said Brennan, meaning it could shape perceptions of a candidate’s character or ideology and could “impact voter trust”.

Other such ads showed Sherrod Brown, a Senate Democratic candidate from the state of Ohio, as the last guest at a party, having overstayed his welcome.

James Talarico, a Senate Democratic candidate from the state of Texas, was shown in a blue dress similar to the character Maria from the movie The Sound of Music, while Mike Rogers, a Senate Republican candidate from Michigan, appeared as a superhero.

In San Francisco, when Democratic California state Senator Scott Wiener released an AI chatbot in the high-profile race to succeed House Speaker Emeritus Nancy Pelosi, who represents the tech-industry city in Congress, it drew an immediate backlash.

The chatbot answered around 5,000 questions about his opponent, Connie Chan, parodying her record of ostensibly blocking real estate development in the city, her accent as well as her naturalized citizenship. The move sparked criticism for being bigoted and Wiener withdrew the chatbot, saying that while it was innovative, “it missed the mark”.

Deepfake ads have emerged in a landscape that aims to protect political speech, including when done through parody. While there is no federal law regulating ads made with AI deepfakes, 31 states have passed their own laws calling for ads made using AI to be labelled.

“State laws do what they can without encroaching on the First Amendment,” said Ilana Beller, director of State AI Governance and Policy at Public Citizen, a Washington, DC, based consumer rights advocacy group. “There is still a need for a federal law,” she said.

Adam Rose, chief operating officer of Starling Lab, a research centre on technology and human rights co-founded by Stanford University and the University of Southern California, said some changes made by AI could just be colour or voice correction that the government does not need to label. AI-generated ads should not be banned, he said.

Instead, Rose said, candidates are always involved in making “judgement calls” on the ads and these calls reflect on them. For Wiener, Rose said, releasing the chatbot “showed bad judgement. It showed voters something about him”.

Wiener is running to represent San Francisco in the US Congress, a city that is the global epicentre of the AI industry with two of the biggest AI companies, Open AI and Anthropic, based there. The city’s representative will play an important role as legislation around AI emerges, especially as polls show a majority of Americans are more concerned than excited about the technology.

“This is a transition moment as AI is reshaping our society,” says Ian Krager, a spokesperson for Connie Chan. “This race is a harbinger for the country. It is a moment where we can show the world America can lead the world on AI development without asking working people to bear the cost.

“And it is clear Connie Chan is with working families while Scott Wiener is with the AI companies,” he said, citing the AI chatbot.

As a state senator, Wiener drafted a California law last year requiring AI companies to disclose security incidents where autonomous systems created by extremely large AI models are involved in dangerous or harmful incidents. A less stringent version became law last year. His office did not respond to Al Jazeera’s request for comment.

Looking at the final stretch of the November midterms and beyond, Public Citizen’s Beller said there is a need to make labelling of ads that use AI as clear and easily understood as food labels so voters can evaluate them accordingly.

“People need to know to look for labels,” she said, as it’s important to create awareness about AI deepfake ads, especially among younger voters and seniors.

In New York, the Democratic Party has filed a complaint with the state board of elections saying the ads violate disclosure requirements and are “misleading to the voters”. But Blakeman has said that “people find it humorous. They like satire”.

The ads are “trying to get attention when candidates know there is political power to be gained by getting attention”, said NYU’s Brennen.

With AI deepfake ads only growing, some candidates have publicly said they will not use them. “People seem to like [the candidates] for it,” said Beller.

articles.summary: Piyush Goyal says India-US trade talks are progressing, and tighter H-1B visa access could boost India’s talent retention, GCCs and startup ecosystem.
articles.body: Bengaluru: Commerce and industry minister Piyush Goyal said on Friday that talks with the US for a trade deal were progressing steadily and the two sides were working on the fine print of a trade, while asserting that tighter access to H-1B visas can benefit India by encouraging skilled professionals to stay back, bringing more technology work to the country and boosting the startup ecosystem.The minister’s comments come days after USTR Jaimeson Greer said that a deal was not imminent, and FM Nirmala Sitharaman stated that talks had hit a plateau. “Going by what the US itself has said, it has nothing more to add or offer, and the fine print is being worked out,” Goyal said at the ET Startup Awards 2026 held in Bengaluru on Friday.“The key issue is how the US will give us the comparative advantage we had agreed upon in February. That requires legal expertise, which AI cannot provide, because this goes beyond the textbook. That is what we are working on,” he said.The trade minister, who just returned from the US, said several American companies had outlined their plans for India as they looked to tap the Indian talent pool and highlighted the cost advantage here.“Look at the entire ecosystem and you will realise that every H-1B visa not granted is a big win for India,” Goyal said.Tighter H-1B access could give Indian startups, particularly in deep technology, greater momentum, he said, adding that the sector had significant room to grow in India.Goyal said he had never raised the issue of H-1B visas or green cards in his conversations with the US as immigration was not directly related to trade, although the movement of people to deliver services was important.He said a growing share of technology work was coming to Indian cities such as Bengaluru, Hyderabad, Pune, Gurugram and Mumbai, as companies recognised the value of setting up global capability centres (GCCs) in the country.Hiring talent in India would also mean that taxes were paid locally and spending supported domestic businesses, infrastructure and startups.You use AI every day. articles.title: Trump eases Russia sanctions, says Putin will release diesel supplies amid unprecedented price spike
articles.summary: President Donald Trump said Russian President Vladimir Putin would “immediately” release hundreds of thousands of tons of diesel fuel onto the global market.
articles.body: President Donald Trump said Friday that Russian President Vladimir Putin would “immediately” release hundreds of thousands of tons of diesel fuel onto the global market. Trump made the announcement on Truth Social and said the action would will help bring diesel prices down. Since its illegal invasion of Ukraine, wide-ranging sanctions have been applied to Russia. In order to get the diesel fuel moved, the Treasury Department simultaneously announced Friday that it would be easing sanctions on Russia through April 7. “Today, at President Trump’s direction, the Office of Foreign Assets Control (OFAC) is immediately issuing a temporary general license to allow the supply of Russian diesel to the global market,” the Treasury Department said on X. A document posted to the Treasury’s website said that “the sale, delivery, offloading, or importation, including importation into the United States, of diesel fuel of Russian Federation origin are authorized through 12:01 a.m. eastern daylight time, April 7, 2027. In a separate statement, Putin said that he had informed Trump of Russia’s “readiness to supply oil and petroleum products to the US and global markets.” Putin did not offer any specifics, however, such as when a potential release would begin or how much fuel it would entail. Since the start of the Iran war in February, the price of diesel fuel has soared almost 70%, and economists have warned that the price hikes will have wide-ranging inflationary effects on the global economy. In recent weeks, sharp escalations in the Russia-Ukraine war have caused diesel to spike even further, and for multiple weeks the price of diesel set repeated all-time records. After multiple Ukrainian attacks on Russian energy assets earlier this year, the Kremlin in July imposed a diesel fuel export ban. It has since been extended through the end of October. Russian deputy prime minister Alexander Novak told state news agency TASS that his country would immediately begin lifting its export ban as a result of the Trump-Putin agreement. Trump has publicly pleaded with Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy to stop bombing Russia’s diesel refinery plants. “The problem I have with Ukraine and Russia is that, you know, a lot of the diesel comes … from Russia, and the Russia plants are being hit by Ukraine,” Trump told reporters recently. “And I’ve asked President Zelenskyy not to hit the diesel plants.” “That’s what’s driving it up,” Trump said, referring to the cost of diesel. Ukraine, he added, has “Got to stop.” On Sept. 14, Trump claimed that Zelenskyy and Putin had agreed to stop targeting energy infrastructure. Zelenskyy, however, denied that he had agreed to stop targeting Russian energy assets, telling CBS News he would only stop striking oil and gas targets if Russia agreed to the same terms. But the Kremlin has increased its targeting of Ukrainian cities and critical infrastructure this summer and fall. Just hours before Trump’s announcement Friday, Zelenskyy welcomed a delegation of U.S. senators to the presidential palace in Kyiv. “We can only protect ourselves from this terror by working together, and we discussed how the United States can help save lives,” Zelenskyy said on social media. “This is a matter of political will, and it is now important to show leadership and fully cut off the financial flows sustaining Russia’s war machine.” Zelenskyy described Trump’s move to ease sanctions on diesel Friday as “an obvious weakness.” “It plays into Russia’s hands — allowing it to kill more, wage war for longer, have even less respect for America, and inflict even greater losses and damage on the world,” he said. This is not the first time Trump has tried to use U.S. sanctions relief for Russia to help slow rising oil prices. The Treasury Department issued a series of 30-day sanctions waivers for Russian oil on the water this spring. But they expired and largely did not impact the trajectory of oil and gas prices, which have continued rising for months. Diesel futures fell 4% Friday in the wake of Trump’s announcement, but they remain higher by more than 110% since the start of this year. Likewise, the price of crude oil barely budged. Brent crude oil traded around $104 per barrel Friday, down just 0.3% on the day. Trump’s announcement also came just as Ukrainian negotiators departed for the U.S., for a new round of talks aimed at bringing an end to the war with Russia. Special envoy Steve Witkoff and President Donald Trump’s son-in-law Jared Kushner had been expected to lead the discussions. It was unclear late Friday whether they would continue as planned in light of the latest sanctions waiver.

What to know about Trump Accounts, auto-enrollment

President Trump touted his administration’s investment accounts for children earlier this week, as millions of American kids will now be automatically enrolled in the program.

Flanked by administration officials, business leaders and Sen. Ted Cruz (R-Texas) in the Oval Office, the president said the “Trump Accounts” will help children build wealth .

An auto-enrollment feature announced recently by the Treasury Department will result in more than 60 million additional kids having an account.

While experts note Trump Accounts are just one of multiple available for children, the president’s move has received widespread support — including from Democrats normally critical of Trump, such as Govs. Wes Moore (D-Md.) and Gavin Newsom (D-Calif.).

articles.title: Tesla is one of the 'clearest ways to own physical AI,' analyst says
articles.summary: Tesla bull Dan Ives is doubling down on the idea that Tesla is an AI company, not an automaker.
articles.body:
Tesla ( TSLA ) bull Dan Ives is doubling down on the idea that Tesla is an AI company, not an automaker.

The longtime Wedbush analyst now at Yorkville Ives reiterated his Outperform rating and $500 price target on Tesla in a note to clients, arguing that autonomy, robotaxis, and Optimus humanoid robots will increasingly be the primary factors driving the company's value.

"We view Tesla as one of the clearest ways to own physical AI in the public markets," Ives wrote. Tesla stock was up over 2% on Friday.

From Ives's viewpoint , Tesla has built under one roof what most AI and robotics efforts are still assembling from partners: a fleet of several million vehicles generating driving data, the AI models and in-house chips that learn from it, and the manufacturing scale to build the products.

"Investors valuing it primarily as an automaker are pricing a fleet rather than the platform being built on top of it," he said.

Ives calls Full Self-Driving (FSD) the bridge between today's car business and tomorrow's autonomy business. The subscription is already lifting software revenue per vehicle, with an attach rate above 55% on new North American EV sales.

Tesla's robotaxi service now operates in six US cities with paid miles approaching 2.5 million, and a 5,000-vehicle Nevada permit gives it a path to a much larger fleet. Cybercab, the purpose-built driverless vehicle with no steering wheel or pedals, has begun production and is carrying paying passengers in Austin.

Ives said the number to watch is the fleet count, "as unsupervised vehicles move from dozens toward thousands, autonomy moves from optionality to revenue."

Ives uses a sum-of-the-parts valuation based on 2028 revenue estimates, which puts Tesla at roughly 12.2 times revenue vs. a peer median of about 5.3 times. By his math, Tesla's existing businesses are worth about $165 per share if it's valued as a car company. Ives assigns the remaining $335 to autonomy and Optimus.

That means around two-thirds of his Tesla price target focuses on businesses still in their early stages. Ives notes only 45 Cybercabs are authorized for driverless operation in Texas, and Tesla itself expects about 2,500 vehicles in Nevada in year one, half of what the permit allows. And Tesla's second quarter update removed both the Cybertruck and Optimus from its 2026 volume production list.

Regulators are another issue that could impede growth. NHTSA issued a Special Order on Cybercab's self-certification , and Tesla's sworn response was due Sept. 30. No decision has been announced, but an adverse finding could confine Cybercab's operational area.

articles.title: Trump announces Russian diesel deal amid soaring US fuel prices
articles.summary: Russia to supply 300,000 tonnes of diesel immediately, followed by 1.5 million more, as prices soar amid the Iran war.
articles.body:
United States President Donald Trump said that Russia has agreed to supply 300,000 tonnes of diesel fuel to global markets amid discussions with Russian President Vladimir Putin.

“I have just concluded a highly successful discussion with President Vladimir Putin, of Russia, wherein it was agreed that Russia will immediately supply over 300,000 tons of diesel fuel to the American and global marketplace, another 500,000 tons during the month of November, and 1,000,000 tons immediately thereafter,” Trump said in a post on his Truth Social platform.

The president added that Russia would deliver an additional 3 million tonnes of fuel “within a short period of time”. He said that the country would supply 500,000 tonnes in November.

An envoy for Russian President Vladimir Putin, Kirill Dmitriev, praised cooperation between Russia and the United States on diesel and energy in a post on X shortly after.

“Russia-US cooperation on diesel and energy will benefit the world,” Dmitriev wrote on X.

The Kremlin said Putin told Trump in a phone call on Friday that Russia was ready “to supply oil” to the US and world markets.

“The Russian side reaffirmed its readiness to supply oil and oil products to the American and world markets,” the Kremlin said regarding the talks.

The Kremlin said the call between Putin and Trump, which lasted an hour and half, covered large-scale economic initiatives, including Russian fuel supplies.

The read-out from Moscow said Trump welcomed Russia’s involvement in efforts to settle the war with Iran.

Earlier this week, Putin met Iranian President Masoud Pezeshkian in Turkmenistan and told him Russia would “do everything” to help end the war, Russian news agencies reported.

In a call on Wednesday, Putin told Pezeshkian that Moscow was prepared to mediate, according to Iran’s IRNA news agency.

Putin told Trump that Russia would consider when to resume peace talks, the Kremlin said. It added that both leaders were interested in taking part in the Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation (APEC) summit in China in November.

Kremlin aide Yuri Ushakov said Trump warmly congratulated Putin on his birthday during the call and wished him success and wellbeing.

The deal comes despite Ukrainian air strikes, which have taken more than half of the country’s oil refining capacity offline, according to claims made by Ukraine’s Ministry of Defence on Sunday.

The latest announcement comes a week after the G7 countries agreed to release 100 million barrels amid pressure from the White House.

The move also comes as prices of diesel, used in agriculture, heating homes and trucking goods, are near record highs ahead of the November 3 congressional elections that will determine control of Congress.

Diesel prices have been elevated in recent months but have started to decline. The average price for a gallon is $6.27 ($1.66 per litre), according to the American Automobile Association (AAA), which tracks daily petrol prices. That’s down $0.10 from this time last week, but up $5.94 from this time one month ago.

Diesel prices, which can drive inflation, are up 70 percent since the US and Israel’s war on Iran began this year, despite two high-profile recent moves by Trump to boost supplies of the fuel: pressuring allies ‌‌to release emergency reserves and expanding access to tax-exempt red-dyed diesel, which is normally used for farm equipment.

The wars in Iran and Ukraine have triggered an unprecedented global fuel supply crunch.

articles.title: Palantir stock hits all-time high after Wall Street grows bullish on next phase of growth
articles.summary: Palantir stock jumped 3% on Thursday morning, thanks to a bullish thesis and upgrade from Goldman Sachs.
articles.body:
Palantir ( PLTR ) stock rose 5% on Friday, thanks to votes of confidence from Barclays and Goldman Sachs.

On Friday, Barclays initiated coverage of Palantir stock with an Overweight rating and $265 price target. The firm said Palantir and SpaceX ( SPCX ) "have deep competitive moats that enable unparalleled levels of growth and margins."

The call came a day after Goldman's research team, led by Gabriela Borges, upgraded shares of Palantir to a Buy rating from Neutral, with a 12-month price target of $230. At that target, the firm sees 18% upside in Palantir's stock from its Wednesday closing price.

"Our primary takeaway from our most recent set of industry conversations is that the stock is setting up for another phase of outperformance into 2027," the analysts wrote.

They noted that Palantir's total addressable market "may be setting up for another step function change in depth, because of the shift to sovereign AI, bespoke applications, and Palantir's newer verticalization strategy."

Palantir stock surpassed its record high set on Nov. 3 of last year, closing at $208.88.

Goldman also highlighted that Palantir "perfected" the feedback loop between its field team, where engineers are deployed to customer sites to help them create custom software applications, and its product team.

More tech companies are hiring field teams, including Microsoft ( MSFT ), Salesforce ( CRM ), and Snowflake ( SNOW ), but the Goldman team thinks Palantir has a head start in creating AI agents to scale that function.

Adding to the boost in sentiment, veteran tech analyst Dan Ives listed Palantir among his top five tech stock picks for 2027 in a post on X on Tuesday.

"In our view, investors [are] underestimating the scale and scope of this $4 trillion dollar spending wave next few years," Ives wrote.

articles.title: Moderna stock hits 4-year high on planned national cancer vaccine effort
articles.summary: Moderna stock popped 9% on Friday after the New York Times reported new details about an effort to speed up cancer vaccine development. Investors saw the mRN...
articles.body:
Moderna ( MRNA ) stock popped 14% on Friday, reaching its highest level since January 2022, after the New York Times reported new details about an effort to accelerate cancer vaccine development. Investors saw the mRNA biotech company, in particular, as a beneficiary.

Biotech stocks, including Pfizer ( PFE ), BioNTech ( BNTX ), and Merck ( MRK ), rallied on the news. Novavax ( NVAX ) shares surged 15%.

According to the New York Times, the new initiative is a public-private partnership — similar to the effort that produced COVID-19 vaccines — that involves the National Institutes of Health (NIH), the NIH's nonprofit arm, researchers, pharmaceutical and biotech companies, advocacy groups, other nonprofits, and patients.

Stacey Adam, a senior clinical officer at the NIH's foundation, told the New York Times that she expects the program to launch in December. In 2024, the UK launched a similar program, called the Cancer Vaccine Launch Pad .

Cancer vaccines are seen as the next frontier in cancer treatment. But they represent an emerging bet.

Unlike other vaccines, such as the COVID-19 vaccine, which aim to prevent infection, cancer vaccines are designed to target cancer cells in patients who already have the disease.

Moderna is viewed as a leader in the mRNA cancer treatment space. The stock soared in August on positive results for a melanoma treatment , developed with Merck, that showed a positive outcome in a late-stage trial.

articles.summary: Qualified student loan borrowers are facing long waiting periods for Public Service Loan Forgiveness. Here's what to know if you're waiting for your federal...
articles.body:

Thousands of student loan borrowers working toward Public Service Loan Forgiveness (PSLF) are waiting for updates on their loan forgiveness.

Nonprofit and government workers who otherwise qualify for PSLF are facing months-long waiting periods under the PSLF Buyback program, which allows borrowers to buy back months (toward their 120 total monthly payments) that didn't have qualifying payments due to deferment or forbearance.

At the same time, some borrowers aren't seeing updated payment counts after making their last required payment toward the forgiveness program. A recent Business Insider report cited one borrower's Federal Student Aid dashboard, noting that payment counts "have been temporarily paused due to data issues causing count fluctuations."

The resulting limbo is leaving many otherwise-eligible PSLF borrowers without a resolution about their loan forgiveness.

Eligible government and nonprofit workers can qualify for Public Service Loan Forgiveness after working full-time for a qualifying employer for at least 10 years and making 120 monthly student loan payments under a qualifying plan.

The PSLF Buyback program, launched in 2023, helps borrowers who have met the employment requirement for PSLF "buy back" the months their loans were in eligible deferment or forbearance.

With the buyback, those borrowers can also meet the loan repayment requirement for PSLF and qualify for loan forgiveness.

To qualify, applicants must have already worked 120 months (10 years) of eligible employment before applying, and the certified eligible employment must include the months they want to buy back. Only Direct Loans are eligible under the program.

Additionally, borrowers won't be able to buy back months for loans enrolled in the two new repayment plans introduced earlier this year — the Repayment Assistance Plan or Tiered Standard Plan. These are the only two repayment options for new borrowers after July 1, 2026.

After applying, applicants must continue to make student loan payments under qualifying payment plans until their PSLF Buyback is approved. Eligible borrowers will receive a PSLF Buyback Agreement when they're approved and must pay the required amount specified in that agreement within 90 days.

As of April 30 this year, there were 88,000 PSLF Buyback applications pending, according to the Department of Education. The Department says that it includes an estimated 18,000 duplicates. Even so, that still leaves 70,000 pending applications.

According to court filings in an ongoing lawsuit by the American Federation of Teachers against the Department of Education, progress in deciding PSLF Buyback applications has been inconsistent. Here's a snapshot of the first few months of 2026:

January 2026: 2,430 applications decided; 1,980 approved

February 2026: 2,520 applications decided; 2,040 approved

March 2026: 3,280 applications decided; 2,710 approved

April 2026: 6,870 applications decided; 6,600 approved

Between January and April, the number of pending PSLF Buyback applications also increased from 86,520 to 88,000 as the Department continued to receive new applications.

What PSLF Buyback applicants should know

Those awaiting a decision on their PSLF Buyback may continue to face a lengthy holding period.

The Federal Student Aid site doesn't indicate when PSLF Buyback applicants will find out whether they're approved.

"We expect that many people will request buyback, and each account review will need in-depth analysis," the site reads. "You won't be able to check the status of your request, but we will respond to your request by email as soon as possible."

In the meantime, it's important to continue making student loan payments until your application is no longer under review and your buyback is approved.

If the payments you make during this time exceed the required buyback amount in your PSLF Buyback Agreement, you receive after approval (and you have no additional loans), you can get the excess payments refunded.

According to the Federal Student Aid site, you can also contact your student loan service to ask about the status of your application.

articles.title: Rising fuel costs slashed Delta’s profit outlook despite strong demand
articles.summary: Rising fuel prices push Delta’s annual fuel expenses up by $6bn, affecting its profit outlook for 2026.
articles.body:
Delta Air Lines cut its profit forecast despite heightened demand as fuel costs surge across the air travel sector.

The Atlanta-based air carrier said in its third-quarter earnings report released on Friday that it expects its annual fuel costs to jump by $6bn, as ongoing tensions between the United States and Iran have sent fuel prices surging across the global aviation sector.

Overall, US airlines spent nearly $43bn on fuel in the first eight months of the year, a $13.2bn increase from the same period a year earlier.

On Wall Street, Delta cut its earnings outlook for the year to adjusted earnings per share of $5.10 to $5.60, down from its July forecast of $6.50 to $7.50. The midpoint of the new range is below analysts’ average estimate of $5.46, according to LSEG data.

Delta’s stock tumbled in midday trading as the trading week came to a close. It was down 1.1 percent from Friday’s opening price. While the stock has fallen 4.4 percent over the past five days, it has performed well in 2026, gaining nearly 18 percent since the beginning of the year.

CEO Ed Bastian said the airline had raised prices by roughly 20 percent this year and said those prices could be sustained even if fuel prices decline.

Delta Air Lines is the first of the major US airlines to report earnings and is generally more protected from price fluctuations than its competitors because it owns a refinery in Pennsylvania, which it acquired in 2012.

Despite higher prices, demand remains elevated, with 60 percent of flights in the fourth quarter already booked. Delta also announced several new international routes, including Seattle–Tokyo, Japan and Boston–Venice, Italy, as well as Austin-Paris, France, all beginning next year.

Bastian told the Wall Street Journal that holiday bookings also remain strong and that premium travel is growing, with premium seat revenue jumping 18 percent for the quarter compared with the same period last year.

Broadly speaking, premium flights can be a boon for major airlines, and prices in the segment are rising. Average ticket prices for premium seats across major airlines were up 11 percent compared with the same period last year, according to the Airline Reporting Corporation’s monthly report, which tracks airline ticket transactions.

But lower-income consumers are pulling back. US consumer sentiment is slumping, according to the University of Michigan’s Surveys of Consumers, which released its Consumer Sentiment Index on Friday.

“Overall, sentiment for lower-income consumers and those with smaller stock portfolios dropped steeply this month, groups that have fewer resources to weather increases in prices,” Joanne Hsu, director of the Surveys of Consumers, said in the release.

Delta’s report comes as the US summer travel season draws to a close, following reports that lower-income travellers would pull back amid rising prices. In May, 51 percent of Americans earning less than $100,000 annually said travel would be one of the first expenses they would cut, according to a report from consulting firm Deloitte.

United Airlines is the next major carrier expected to report earnings, with results slated for after the market close on October 20. Like Delta, United’s stock was down on Wall Street, falling 0.8 percent from Friday’s opening price.

articles.body: MUMBAI: Banks concluded the first half of FY27 with an acceleration in balance-sheet expansion, as year-on-year credit growth climbed to 19.4% and aggregate deposit growth reached 17.8%, leaving the credit-to-deposit ratio at 81%.Total bank credit stood at over Rs 229.9 lakh crore as of Sept 30, while aggregate deposits reached about Rs 284 lakh crore. Many large banks that have submitted their business figures to the exchanges have attributed the increase to the $133 billion mobilised under the FCNR(B) scheme.The year-on-year deposit growth at the end of the first quarter (June 30 2026) was 13.3% while the growth in advances was 18.6% A year earlier, at the end of Sept 2025, bank credit growth stood at 11.4%, while aggregate deposits grew 9.9%. Time deposits were the primary driver of deposit accretion, contributing Rs 36.3 lakh crore, or 84.5% of total annual deposit growth, to reach Rs 246.6 lakh crore.This represented annual growth of 17.3%, compared with 8.8% a year earlier. Demand deposits rose 21.6%, or Rs 6.6 lakh crore, year-on-year to Rs 37.4 lakh crore, up from growth of 18.5% a year earlier.With credit growth outstripping deposit growth, banks are facing tighter resource constraints, with the credit-to-deposit ratio remaining above 80%. During the fortnight ended Sept 30, 2026, credit expansion lifted the credit-to-deposit ratio to 81%. From 78.9% at the end of Sept 2024, the ratio rose to 80.8% in March 2025. articles.title: Now, RBI puts CRR and bond sale into play
articles.summary: MUMBAI: RBI has tightened daily cash reserve requirements for banks, impounding an additional Rs 1 lakh crore, and has announced a Rs 25,000 crore bond
articles.body: MUMBAI: RBI has tightened daily cash reserve requirements for banks, impounding an additional Rs 1 lakh crore, and has announced a Rs 25,000 crore bond sale, moves that will drain liquidity from the banking system and put upward pressure on overnight money market rates amid pressure on prices as well as the exchange rate from the intensifying conflict in West Asia.The liquidity-draining measure will hasten the transmission of the 25-basis-point repo rate cut announced by the central bank on Oct 7.RBI has raised the minimum daily cash reserve ratio (CRR) requirement from 90% to 99% of the prescribed level, effective from the fortnight beginning Oct 16, 2026. The open market operation (OMO) sale auction of govt of India securities worth Rs 25,000 crore is on Oct 13. Using aggregate deposits of around Rs 284 lakh crore as a rough proxy, the maximum additional daily CRR balance works out to approximately Rs 1 lakh crore (with daily CRR increasing from 3.6% to 3.96% of deposits).Banks are required to maintain a CRR of 4% of their deposits. The statutory ratio remains unchanged, but RBI has reduced the flexibility banks have in meeting the requirement during the fortnight. Previously, banks could maintain at least 90% of the prescribed CRR on each day, provided their average daily balance over the reporting fortnight met the full requirement.Under the revised norms, banks must maintain at least 99% of the prescribed CRR every day while continuing to meet the full requirement on average over the fortnight.This will require banks to keep a larger portion of their deposits with RBI on a daily basis, reducing the funds available to meet short-term liquidity needs. Dealers said that since banks cannot predict the extent of deposits accurately, they need to err on the side of caution to avoid defaulting on CRR and end up maintaining more than the statutory requirement.

articles.title: Religious, spiritual & astrology apps see nearly 30cr downloads in Jan-Sept
articles.summary: NEW DELHI: From listening to bhajans and reading the Bible to finding the direction of Mecca or discovering what the stars have in store, Indians are
articles.body: NEW DELHI: From listening to bhajans and reading the Bible to finding the direction of Mecca or discovering what the stars have in store, Indians are increasingly turning to smartphones for matters of faith and fortune. Religious, spiritual and astrology apps recorded nearly 30 crore downloads in the first nine months of 2026, emerging as fast-growing segments of India's app economy.According to data shared exclusively with TOI by market intelligence firm Sensor Tower, astrology apps registered 15 crore downloads between Jan and Sept, a 75% jump over last year. Religious and spiritual apps clocked 14.6 crore downloads, up 47%. Together, the categories surpassed their combined 24.8 crore downloads in the whole of 2025 and touched nearly 30 crore downloads.The digital devotion wave is cutting across religions. articles.title: Trump announces Russia will release 2.2 million barrels of diesel 'immediately,' with more to follow
articles.summary: In a social media post, President Trump said he'd struck a deal with Vladimir Putin for a quick release of 300,000 tons of diesel from Russia.
articles.body:
President Trump announced on Friday that Russia will "immediately" release hundreds of thousands of tons of diesel into global markets, in an effort to combat spiraling prices around the globe.

In a social media post, Trump said he'd struck a deal with Russian President Vladimir Putin for a quick release of 300,000 tons (about 2.2 million barrels), followed by another 500,000 in November and 1 million tons "immediately thereafter." That comes out to about 13.5 million barrels.

"Between our TOTAL CONTROL of the Strait of Hormuz, and this great announcement on Russian Energy, Diesel Prices for Americans and, indeed, the World, will be COMING DOWN, IN RECORD NUMBERS, AND FAST!" Trump wrote on Truth Social .

Diesel prices have soared in recent weeks, averaging $6.28 per gallon on Friday, according to AAA. The administration has pulled other levers in an attempt to reverse the rise, with just weeks to go before the midterm elections, in which cost-of-living and economic issues are at the forefront of voters' minds.

Rob Thummel, senior portfolio manager at Tortoise Capital, told Yahoo Finance on Friday that the release of Russian oil onto global markets should bring some short-term price relief but is not a long-term fix.

"This is not going to dramatically change the price of diesel, but I do think it will push the price of diesel down, you know, over the next at least few weeks," Thummel said.

The initial 2.2 million barrels is less diesel than the US uses for transportation in a single day .

After initially floating a domestic ban on diesel exports , Trump backed off that notion and later joined a global agreement by G7 nations to release up to 100 million barrels of emergency oil and diesel over the next four months.

He also relaxed restrictions on red-dyed diesel, an untaxed fuel that is used primarily in agriculture. Experts say that move is likely to bring some relief to farmers but may not help America's truckers.

To enable the deal with Moscow, the Treasury Department relaxed sanctions on Russian energy, allowing it to be imported into the US . A document posted to Treasury's website eases the restrictions on Russian diesel through April 7, 2027.

Patrick De Haan, GasBuddy head of petroleum analysis, posted on X that he's skeptical about Russia's ability to deliver that much supply.

"It may be difficult to achieve. The psychological impact may reduce prices temporarily but it'll take more time to determine if Russia has such ability," he wrote. "Some impact short term, perhaps 10-20c/gal."
